passage:
In science class, students watched a video about ice cores. Scientists drill deep into old ice and study air bubbles trapped inside it.
The idea amazed Daniel. He had thought ice was only frozen water. Now he learned that ice could hold clues about ancient air, volcanoes, and climate.
The teacher compared an ice core to a history book written by weather. Each layer formed at a different time.
After class, Daniel looked at the ice in his drink differently. It would melt in minutes, but ice in polar regions could remember thousands of years.
Science sometimes begins when an ordinary thing becomes less ordinary.
